Question
========
The `ggsave()` function is a convenient way to save a ggplot2 plot to a file - it is essentially a wrapper around the underlying graphic device driver. Besides the plot itself (which defaults to the last plot generated), what is the only other argument you always have to supply to `ggsave()`?


Solution
========
The file name. `ggsave()` makes reasonable guesses for almost everything else - the plot to save (it defaults to `last_plot()`), the image size, and even the graphic device, which is inferred from the file extension you use (for example `.pdf`, `.png` or `.eps`). The one thing it cannot guess is what the file should be called, so the file name always has to be provided.


Meta-information
================
exname: mandatory argument of ggsave
extype: string
exsolution: filename
